questions.q: What is the main difference between FI and CO?
options: FI is the official books for outsiders; CO is the internal view of costs and results for managers
FI is for claims; CO is for sales
FI is only used in Denmark; CO is used everywhere
FI handles salaries; CO handles bank statements
questions.reason: FI (Financial Accounting) produces the balance sheet, P&L and statutory reports for authorities, auditors and owners. CO (Controlling) shows managers which department or line of business costs or earns what.

questions.q: Jonas Krogh wants to know whether motor or home insurance has the better result. Which part of FICO answers that?
options: CO, using profit centres such as PC-MOTOR and PC-HOME
FI, using only the bank account
The FS-CD dunning run
The chart of accounts alone
questions.reason: Result per line of business is an internal, management question. CO answers it with profit centres.

questions.q: Who are the main readers of FI reports such as the balance sheet and P&L?
options: Finanstilsynet, Skattestyrelsen, auditors and owners
Only the claims handlers
Only the IT department
Policyholders checking their premium
questions.reason: FI looks outward: its reports follow law and accounting standards and are read by people outside the company's management.

questions.q: What does SAP FS-CD send to the general ledger?
options: Daily totals of premiums, claims and commission postings
One GL posting for every policyholder letter
Nothing; FS-CD does not connect to FI
Only the bank statement
questions.reason: FS-CD is the sub-ledger with the detail per policyholder. It posts daily totals to the GL, for example to the premium receivables account 140000.

questions.q: Why does a FICO BA need to understand the policy system, claims system and FS-CD?
options: Most FI and CO postings are created automatically by events in those systems
Because FI cannot post anything by itself
Because they replace FI in S/4HANA
Because FICO has no GL accounts of its own
questions.reason: Billing a policy, paying a claim or running payroll all create postings in FI and CO, so the cause of a number often starts outside finance.

questions.q: How are claims payments to garages and policyholders handled at Nordica?
options: Through the claims system and FS-CD, not FI accounts payable
Through FI accounts payable like rent
By typing them into FB50 by hand
Through the controlling area
questions.reason: Ordinary suppliers such as IT and rent go through FI accounts payable. Claims payments go through the claims system and FS-CD.

questions.q: What is a company code?
options: One legal company with its own balance sheet and P&L, such as NF01
A password for logging on to SAP
A cost centre for the head office
The number of a policy
questions.reason: The company code is the smallest unit that must produce full legal accounts. Nordica Forsikring A/S is company code NF01.

questions.q: What is a chart of accounts such as NFKP?
options: The list of all GL accounts a company code may use
A diagram of the company's departments
The list of open posting periods
A bank's list of transactions
questions.reason: The chart of accounts is like a dictionary of where money can be recorded, for example 110000 Bank or 470000 Rent.

questions.q: Nordica uses a calendar fiscal year with 12 normal periods and 4 special periods. What are the special periods for?
options: Year-end corrections after December, without reopening December
Extra months for leap years
Postings in foreign currency
Payroll only
questions.reason: Special periods 13 to 16 hold year-end adjustments such as audit corrections or a changed reserve estimate, so December stays clean but the annual figures include them.

questions.q: Which transaction is used to open and close posting periods?
options: OB52
FB03
FS00
FBL3N
questions.reason: OB52 controls which periods are open. If period 3 is closed, a posting dated in March is refused.

questions.q: What is the relationship between controlling area NF00 and company code NF01?
options: NF01 is assigned to NF00; a controlling area can hold several company codes
NF00 is a GL account inside NF01
They are two names for the same thing
NF00 is the bank account of NF01
questions.reason: The controlling area is the unit in which CO works. Company codes are assigned to it, and one controlling area can contain several company codes.

questions.q: What is a cost centre?
options: A place where costs happen and someone is responsible, such as 1000 Claims handling
A line of business you want a result figure for
A bank account
A type of supplier invoice
questions.reason: Cost centres collect costs by responsibility. Nordica has 1000 Claims handling, 2000 Sales and distribution, 3000 Administration and 4100 IT.

questions.q: What is a profit centre at an insurer like Nordica?
options: A part of the business you want a result for, usually a line of business such as PC-MOTOR
A department that only has costs
A GL account for premiums
The bank where profits are kept
questions.reason: Profit centres show results by line of business, region or business unit. Nordica uses PC-MOTOR and PC-HOME.

questions.q: Which kinds of account go UP with a debit?
options: Assets and expenses
Liabilities and revenue
Equity and revenue
Liabilities and equity
questions.reason: Assets (such as the bank or premium receivables) and expenses (such as rent) increase on the debit side. Liabilities, equity and revenue increase on the credit side.

questions.q: How does SAP usually show a credit amount in line item reports?
options: As a negative number, so every document adds up to 0.00
As a positive number in red
It does not show credits at all
As a percentage
questions.reason: Debits are positive and credits negative. The bank line of the rent document shows -50,000.00, and the document balances to 0.00.

questions.q: Why can Maria not post directly to account 160000 Trade payables?
options: It is a reconciliation account, updated only through postings to suppliers
It is closed in OB52
It belongs to the controlling area only
It is a P&L account
questions.reason: A reconciliation account summarises a group of suppliers. Posting to the supplier updates 160000 automatically, so the GL always agrees with the supplier list. Account 140000 works the same way for FS-CD.

questions.q: In the FB03 screen, what do posting keys 40 and 50 mean?
options: 40 is a debit to a GL account, 50 is a credit to a GL account
40 is a premium bill, 50 is a claim payment
40 and 50 are cost centre numbers
40 means posted, 50 means reversed
questions.reason: Posting keys say whether a line is a debit or a credit and what kind of account it is. 40 and 50 are the GL account debit and credit keys.

questions.q: The rent invoice is dated 25.02.2026 and posted on 01.03.2026. Which month does the cost count in?
options: March, because the posting date decides the period
February, because the document date decides the period
Both months, half each
Neither, until it is paid
questions.reason: The posting date decides the period. 01.03.2026 falls in period 3 (March). The document date is the date on the original paper.

questions.q: In the rent document, why does the 470000 Rent line have cost centre 3000, but the bank line has none?
options: Rent is a cost, so CO needs to know which department carries it; a bank account is not a cost
Bank lines are never shown in FB03
Cost centre 3000 only exists for the bank
It is a mistake that must be corrected
questions.reason: Cost lines need a cost object for CO. Balance sheet lines such as the bank do not.

questions.q: How do you correct a posted journal entry that was wrong?
options: Post a reversal document; the original is never deleted
Delete it in FB03
Change the amount in FS10N
Close the period in OB52
questions.reason: Posted documents are permanent. A reversal posts the opposite signs and the original is marked as reversed, so the audit trail stays complete.

questions.q: What is the Universal Journal (table ACDOCA) in S/4HANA?
options: One table where every posting line is stored with both its FI and CO information
A separate CO table that must be reconciled with FI every month
A list of all users who posted documents
A Fiori app for printing policies
questions.reason: In S/4HANA every line item lands in ACDOCA with company code, GL account, amount, cost centre, profit centre and more, so FI and CO cannot disagree.

questions.q: In S/4HANA, where do you maintain a cost element such as Rent?
options: In FS00, as a GL account with a cost element category
In OB52
In FB03
In a separate CO-only master that has no GL account
questions.reason: In S/4HANA cost elements are GL accounts. FS00 holds the cost element category, primary (like rent) or secondary (like 940000 IT assessment).

questions.q: Insurance is VAT-exempt in Denmark. What does this mean for Nordica's purchases, such as the laptop invoice with 25% VAT?
options: The VAT can generally not be deducted, so it becomes part of the cost
The VAT is posted to an input VAT account and claimed back
The VAT is ignored and not recorded anywhere
The VAT is paid by the supplier
questions.reason: Because Nordica charges no VAT on premiums, it generally cannot deduct VAT on purchases. The full DKK 100,000 is cost, which is why there is no input VAT account. Confirm details with the tax team.

questions.q: Hygge Hjem's premium is DKK 120,000 plus 1.1% insurance tax. What does the customer owe?
questions.reason: 1.1% of 120,000 is 1,320, so the total is 121,320. No VAT is added because insurance is VAT-exempt.

questions.q: In the premium posting, where does the DKK 1,320 insurance tax go?
options: Credit to 290100 Insurance tax payable, a debt to Skattestyrelsen
Credit to 300000 Gross written premium
Debit to 470000 Rent
Credit to 110000 Bank
questions.reason: Nordica collects the tax for Skattestyrelsen. It is not income, so it sits as a liability until paid.

questions.q: What is the unearned premium reserve (UPR)?
options: The part of billed premium that covers future months of cover
Money set aside for claims that are not yet reported
The insurance tax owed to Skattestyrelsen
The premium the customer has not paid yet
questions.reason: Written premium is what was billed; earned premium is the part for time already passed. The rest is the UPR. Claims not yet reported are IBNR, a different reserve.

questions.q: What does IBNR mean?
options: Incurred but not reported: a claim has happened but nobody has told Nordica yet
Insurance bought and not received
Invoice booked, no reference
Interest bearing net receivable
questions.reason: IBNR and RBNS (reported but not settled) are the two parts of the claims reserves. The actuary estimates them.

questions.q: In the March example, total debits are DKK 294,320. What must total credits be?
options: DKK 0
questions.reason: In double entry every posting balances, so the total of all debits always equals the total of all credits.

questions.q: In the five postings, by how much does the bank balance go down?
options: DKK 68,000 (rent and telephony)
questions.reason: Only the rent (50,000) and the telephony (18,000) are paid from the bank. The premium and the laptop invoice are still open items.

questions.q: Which transaction shows a GL account's balance period by period, for example how much rent was posted so far this year?
options: FS10N
FB50
OB52
FS00
questions.reason: FS10N shows GL account balances per period. FBL3N shows the individual line items behind them.
